Replay

Local diagnostic overlay

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Audit boundaries and ownershipIntegrated examples and acceptance

Use the opt-in Debug_Overlay to inspect runtime counters and audit whether recent recorded inputs reproduce the retained state and events. It is a presentation/debugging component, separate from simulation state and wire schemas. It sends no requests to peers, writes no files, and does not issue game actions or apply corrected state.

Odin
// In the owning node's ready hook, only when debugging is requested:
debuggd.debug_overlay_init(&debug, owner, true)

// After the application's normal simulation/session pump:
debuggd.debug_timeline_frame(&debug, &timeline) // local value timeline
// or:
debuggd.debug_session_frame(&debug, &session)   // Session facade

// During teardown:
debuggd.debug_overlay_destroy(&debug)

F8 hides/shows the panel. F9 audits recent retained history while the panel is visible. Status refresh is limited to four times per second; disabled/hidden panels do not format status snapshots. An audit is an explicit synchronous operation, capped at 120 ticks by the convenience drivers. Large simulations can still pause visibly during that requested work; use debug_audit with a smaller window when appropriate. It is not a per-frame determinism check.

The local timeline view shows epoch, head, confirmation, retained slots and its latest replayable window. Session views add role/phase, rejection, local seat or peer count, traffic totals, correction/replay counts, deferred snapshots and resync status. Traffic values are lifetime application counters, not bandwidth rates or measured RTT. No token, bearer credential or hidden peer-state exchange is involved.

Audit boundaries and ownership#

audit_window locates the latest bounded replayable suffix and stops at an initial or authority-corrected checkpoint. The checkpoint's generating input is unknown locally, so auditing across it would be a false reproducibility test. audit_recent uses that window with the owned capture API. A checkpoint without a replayed suffix reports Initial_Frame; missing input/history is not approximated.

The overlay formats the first captured state/event failure through the canonical field schema. It reports the failing tick, preceding frame tick, expected/replayed values and event counts. Display limits are explicit. Unsupported schema types remain a diagnostic message rather than being coerced into an approximate format. The captured values are independent copies and are released after formatting; the panel owns only the resulting text and its UI nodes.

These audits test local reproduction from recorded inputs. They do not prove cross-machine determinism, undo illegal external side effects or compare a hidden remote world. Authority data in a local audit should remain in trusted developer workflows. The panel is not a production player-facing debugging or administration permission system.

Integrated examples and acceptance#

Replay Hello's local scene and Replay Cavecrawl expose debug_enabled in the inspector. They also accept REPLAY_DEBUG=1 (or ?debug=1 in a browser launch). The regular scene defaults leave the overlay unallocated. Original examples and Kit remain separately available.

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_debug/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_debug/ports_run.sh

The first gate injects a deliberately illegal external-state change into a small fixture, presses F9 and checks the exact inventory[1]: 7 -> 8 report at tick 2. Recorded inventory remains 7. It verifies hidden-panel behavior, a subsequent successful audit, clean teardown and WASM checking. The port gate exercises the same controls on Hello and real host/client Cavecrawl processes; the client audit starts after its correction boundary. A rendered panel capture is retained in the live diagnostic evidence.

The separate local history dock supports retained-frame inspection, field editing, original-future resume and explicit branching in Replay Hello. Portable recordings retain replayable history windows for later verification. The audit overlay remains read-only; graph views and richer Room/P2P-specific panels remain additional roadmap work.
